Cyber Attack Disrupts Jordan’s Tourism Industry, Forces Closures and Cancellations

AMMAN, June 17 – A major cyber attack targeting firms in Jordan’s tourism sector has forced multiple tourist sites to close and left hundreds of workers unable to access key systems, industry officials said Monday.

Management systems at several leading tour operators, travel agencies and heritage site offices were locked in what appears to be a widespread ransomware attack, according to the Jordan Tourism Association. The breach began late Sunday night and is ongoing, preventing staff from processing bookings, issuing visitor tickets, or managing reservations.

“We are facing an unprecedented disruption,” said Nidal Haddad, spokesperson for the association. “Our members’ staff are unable to access booking platforms or even basic communications. Tourist site entry systems have been disabled, forcing us to close several major attractions for the day.”

Impacted sites include popular destinations around Petra, Jerash, and the Dead Sea region. The full number of affected locations has not been confirmed. Local operators said hundreds of pre-booked tours were cancelled or postponed, with visitors turned away at entrances Monday morning.

“We were about to start welcoming groups for the day when all our computers froze,” said Lina Harb, manager at Golden Oasis Tours. “We couldn’t print tickets, access itineraries, or coordinate with guides. Many staff simply had to stop work.”

The Jordan Tourism Workers Union estimated that at least 1,200 employees across the sector were directly affected on Monday, with some unable to clock in or complete their shifts due to the IT outage.

Officials said the attack has not yet been contained and stressed that IT teams are working around the clock to restore systems. “We are cooperating with cybersecurity experts and authorities,” said Haddad. “Our priority is to secure our data and resume normal operations as quickly as possible.”

The Ministry of Tourism urged patience from visitors and said updates would follow as the situation develops. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
